readme: Detectors with NO production caller that are meant to have none. audit-guard-contract.ps1 fails on any detector nothing in production calls, because a guard nobody runs is not a guard - audit-unit-basis-outlier.ps1 sat dead from 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-08 while the board published butter priced from a bottle of pancake syrup, and audit-script-census stayed green the whole time because the one executable naming it was its own test. Reachability now distinguishes a PRODUCTION caller from a TEST caller, and this file is the written statement of which detectors are unwired on purpose. Keyed by NAME alone, unlike the drift allowlists: what is blessed here is a permanent property of the script (it is a manual diagnostic), not a transient state a content hash should re-arm on. Adding a line is a decision someone defends in a diff. If the honest answer is 'this should run', wire it into the chain instead - that is what audit-count-gpu.ps1 and audit-prompt-backup.ps1 got on 2026-08-08.

manual.name: audit-full.ps1
manual.reason: A deep read-only exploration of the whole board that prints findings by section for a human to read. It asserts nothing and exits 0 regardless, so wiring it into the chain would add runtime and produce no verdict. Diagnostic, run by hand when investigating.

manual.name: test-unitprice.ps1
manual.reason: A debugging tool: runs the engine's own Get-ItemPrice / Get-UnitPrice against SPECIFIC rows named on the command line and shows which branch fired. It has no default work list, so an unattended run would examine nothing. Manual by construction.

manual.name: audit-ff-missing-products.ps1
manual.reason: Written 2026-07-14 for one incident: a partial Family Fare pull overwrote the full catalogue and 104 held products vanished. The recurring protection for that class now lives in audit-ff-carry.ps1 and the everyday-file PARTIAL-OVERWRITE rule, both of which DO run. Kept as a forensic tool for the same shape, not a standing check.

manual.name: verify-starthere.ps1
manual.reason: A one-shot that verified the /start-here/ page published correctly on 2026-07-26. It checks a single page that has since been stable, and the general case is now covered by audit-ghost-drift. Finished; kept because re-verifying that page by hand is occasionally useful.

manual.name: test-rollback-ttl.ps1
manual.reason: A FIXTURE TEST, not a detector. It exercises rollback-ttl-lib against frozen synthetic dates and reads no live data at all, so there is nothing for a production run to detect - running it in the daily chain would assert the same six things about the same constants every morning. It IS run: test-auditors calls it, which is the correct home for a unit test. The thing it protects (first_seen must never re-anchor, or a 30-day TTL becomes infinite) is enforced in production by rollback-ttl-lib itself, which the builders call.

manual.name: test-capture-builders.ps1
manual.reason: A FIXTURE TEST, not a detector - same class as test-rollback-ttl.ps1 above, and blessed for the same reason. It builds a sandbox of fake captures and fake builders, extracts capture-run.ps1's builder block by marker and runs it against them. It reads no live data and detects nothing about the estate, so a production caller would assert the same ten things about the same fakes every morning. It IS run: test-auditors calls it. What it protects - that the 2026-08-23 three-pass restructure (serial existence checks, a fan-out over the first-stage builders, serial verdict handling) still keeps a missing capture outstanding, names a failed builder, skips stage 2 after a failed stage 1, and judges stage 2 on evidence rather than exit code - is enforced in production by capture-run.ps1 itself on every capture. Declared here on the day it was added, rather than left to show up as audit-guard-contract's seventh DEAD line.

manual.name: test-ad-match.ps1
manual.reason: A FIXTURE TEST, not a detector - same class as test-rollback-ttl.ps1 and test-capture-builders.ps1 above, blessed for the same reason. It drives ad-match-lib against frozen synthetic ad lines to prove a sale cell cannot take the window of whichever same-price ad line happens to come first. It reads no live data, so a production caller would assert the same things about the same fixtures every morning. It IS run: test-auditors calls it, which is the correct home for a unit test. What it protects is enforced in production by ad-match-lib itself, which the builders call.

manual.name: test-commit-size-gate.ps1
manual.reason: A FIXTURE TEST of the commit-size gate's predicate, run against synthetic diffs rather than the repo. capture-run.ps1 describes the gate in prose but does not invoke this file - only the LIVE gate - which is why reachability sees no production caller. It IS run: test-auditors calls it. Note the census matches on the full 'test-commit-size-gate.ps1' including the extension, so a prose mention of the bare name does not and should not count as a caller.

manual.name: test-hyvee-tag-check.ps1
manual.reason: A FIXTURE TEST covering two frozen Hy-Vee rules: a price below the store shelf tag is refused, a real promotion is not, and no script is pinned to the retired Omaha #01 store. Fixtures only - it reads no live capture. It IS run: test-auditors calls it. The live half is enforced in production by the Hy-Vee puller and the shelf-tag guard.

manual.name: test-price-split.ps1
manual.reason: A FIXTURE TEST of price-split-lib: the everyday/ad separation Brad called non-negotiable, proved against synthetic rows in both directions. It reads no live board. It IS run: test-auditors calls it. Production enforcement lives in price-split-lib and compare-deals, which every build calls.

manual.name: test-commodity-rules.ps1
manual.reason: A FIXTURE TEST of individual commodity include/exclude rules, frozen against REAL product names. Written 2026-08-24 after the Recipe Hunter's 6b run found chicken-thighs excluding \b(drumsticks?)\b while its own label read 'Chicken Thighs / Drumsticks', so the board answered 'chicken drumsticks' with seven stores of THIGHS. It shipped with NO caller at all - the census listed it as an ORPHAN and guard-contract as DEAD. Wired into test-auditors on 2026-08-25, which is the correct home for a fixture suite; recorded here because a test-only caller is still not a production one, exactly like the entries above.

manual.name: verify-debt.ps1
manual.reason: NOT A GROCERY DETECTOR AT ALL - it lives in .claude\skills\lesson\ and belongs to the lesson skill. It is a manual one-shot that WRITES a sample debt scenario into the live Google Sheets debt calculator and reads the computed outputs back to verify the sheet's formulas. It must NEVER be wired into an automated chain: it mutates a production spreadsheet Brad's readers use. It looks DEAD to audit-guard-contract because the only thing that invokes it is the skill's Markdown, and the reachability scan reads .ps1/.js/.yml and not .md - so every skill-owned helper will always appear dead. Recorded rather than excluded, so the decision is visible in a diff.

manual.name: verify-savings.ps1
manual.reason: The savings-goal twin of verify-debt.ps1 above, in .claude\skills\lesson\, and blessed for exactly the same reasons: a manual one-shot that writes sample goals into the live Google Sheets savings tracker and reads the results back, unreachable to a scan that cannot read the skill Markdown that calls it, and dangerous to automate because it writes to a production sheet.
